headline: Man Utd: A defence with relegation all over it as Pochettino suffers nightmare start
author: Simon Stone

paragraphs.text: When he spoke to the media after Manchester United's four-goal defeat at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino was asked about his side's woeful defensive record.
The United head coach dismissed the question. "I can only talk about what has happened since I have been here," he argued.
Seven days on, the goals conceded is now up 10 in three games after a 4-0 humiliation at home to Brentford, the subject was raised again.
"Well, I think it's by improving," said the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea manager.
"It's a question that, when you concede against Liverpool, and play with 10 men after eight minutes, it's a 'worse impossible' situation.
"[But] how? It's [by] working. It's trying to improve. It's trying to find the right combinations between the players. To keep testing, keep proving, keep pushing. There is not another way.
"We cannot stop to train. We cannot stop to watch clips. We cannot stop to do the review analysis. We try to give the tools to keep improving.
"It is a tough moment, of course. You say to me, 'Tougher than you expect?' Of course, yes, because we never expect this type of result.
"But that is the reality and we need to accept the reality. We are here for that."
There are plenty of statistics attaching themselves to Manchester United at the moment - none of them good, and all pointing towards a team in real danger of relegation.
But for all the unhappy historic milestones, this one should be ringing alarm bells loudest at Old Trafford.
Since the 1-1 draw at Leeds on 18 October, Manchester United have played eight times in all competitions and conceded 25 goals. In their past four, they have conceded an incredible 14.
United's sorry statistics

• Manchester United have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their opening 12 league games of a season for the first time since 1930-31, a campaign in which they finished bottom of the top flight.

• They are the first team in Premier League history to concede at least twice in seven consecutive halves of football. They have also conceded at least four goals in three successive league games for the first time since November and December 1961.
• Pochettino is only the second manager in Premier League history to lose each of his first two matches in charge by four or more goals, after Dave Jones with Wolverhampton Wanderers in August 2003.
• Of the 27 teams who have taken eight points from their first 11 games in the Premier League era, 17 have been relegated.
• United conceded 50 Premier League goals last season and did not sign a defender in the summer.
• Four of the five defenders used by United on Saturday started the 4-0 defeat at Brentford more than four years ago.
In the analysis of his own side's performance, Brentford manager Keith Andrews made a pertinent point.
"The development of our team is being able to deal with getting punched on the nose, getting up and not let it affect you too badly," he said.
Pochettino cannot say the same.

Not for the first time this season, Manchester United played well - as at Hull on the opening day, they lost this match despite having a better xG (expected goals) - but conceded a soft opener and never recovered.

"The moment we concede the goal - and we should not concede this goal - the game goes difficult," Pochettino told BBC Match of the Day. "The intensity. The nerves. This situation, a situation like this, is affecting your confidence. But we need to be united, stay together and keep pushing."
Later, speaking in his post-match media conference, Pochettino expanded.
"We need to keep united and, of course, tell the truth to everyone, and accept that circumstances are really tough," he said.

"It's not only one thing we need to help and support and to improve, it's many areas. We are working on it. Maybe we are not seeing the result because always it's the same. You can improve things, you can do things in a different way, you can do things, but after, if you don't win, it's like you did nothing.

"But it's not like this. In football, always you pay after. You can do something not right and get results. Then when you are going down, you start to do the right things and you need to wait to get the reward.
"That is the difficult thing that in football it's not easy to understand."

Manchester United will drop to the foot of the table if Crystal Palace beat Hull at Selhurst Park on Sunday. Palace could also leapfrog United on Wednesday, when their match at Chelsea begins 45 minutes before their game at Newcastle.
It is one of six more Premier League games they have to play before the transfer window opens.

Yet, more than £1.1bn in debt and having borrowed £10m just after paying the £9m that secured the services of Pochettino and his staff from US Soccer, the answer to United's problems cannot solely be found in new players.
"What do people expect from a coach that arrived 10 days ago?" he said. "Are we going to change 25, 26 players?
"Do you think that we are going to help Manchester United blaming the players because of that situation we are now living?"
Is there a way out of this mess?
Manchester United feel like a shell of a great club at the moment.
The green and gold protests against the ownership continued. Songs were sung in support of the axed Michael Carrick and against director of football Jason Wilcox.
After the fourth goal, home supporters in front of the directors' box turned to vent their anger at Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada. They did the same after the final whistle.
Behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson and David Gill, manager and chief executive in an era of glory that now feels so long ago watched on. Who knows what they must be thinking, but it cannot be positive.

There is no hiding from United's plight. Without a swift form reversal, they are heading down to the second tier for the first time since 1973-74. For one of the world's richest clubs, that would be catastrophic.
"They are in a relegation battle, no doubt about it," former England midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport.

"Today's defeat will have been a real eye-opener for Mauricio Pochettino. It showed him he can't go after sides and leave that team so exposed - he just doesn't have the players. You just cannot continually be that wide open and concede that many chances and goals.

"They are in a relegation battle so he's got to devise a more pragmatic defensive tactical plan, irrelevant of the perception of how a Manchester United team should play. They have no choice but to adapt.

"No opposition is respecting them. As soon as they concede they just deflate, the fans get angsty and the players lose confidence. The only way to get out of such a bad position is to become defensively really good. You can only do that if you have numbers behind the ball and defend for your lives.

"Any group of players can be hard to beat if the distances between defenders are small, if you are disciplined, if you are compact and you play deep. Pochettino has got to be humble and get his team to nick some draws, keep some clean sheets and get some confidence before he even thinks about playing front-foot, creative football again.
"If they go toe-to-toe with anyone at the moment they lose, simple as that."
